punchline: Lincoln put three men who had lost to him in his cabinet, and a month later one of them proposed to run policy himself.
thirty_sec: In 1860 Lincoln beat Seward, Chase and Bates for the Republican nomination, then invited all three into his cabinet. Each thought he was better suited to be president. A month into the job, Seward sent a memo implying he could direct policy. Lincoln kept him but made clear the president decides. Seward ended up one of Lincoln's closest friends. Doris Kearns Goodwin tells it in Team of Rivals.
key_contrast: Rivals at the table, one decider
